question: Should OpenClaw adopt this experiment-gated, versioned grouped Claw update-planning CLI and ownership contract in core before the Claws RFC is accepted?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent, but code review cannot decide whether the project should permanently own the new CLI, schema, provenance, shared-package, MCP, workspace, and upgrade semantics.

options.title: Gate on RFC acceptance
options.body: Keep this PR open and unmerged until maintainers accept or narrow the RFC and the prerequisite lifecycle contract lands.

options.title: Sponsor the current contract
options.body: Explicitly approve the present experiment-gated command and versioned plan semantics, then review the stacked prerequisite and follow-up as one compatibility program.

options.title: Narrow the first update slice
options.body: Retain only the ownership domains maintainers are ready to support and defer contested package, MCP, cron, or restoration semantics.

recommendation.title: Gate on RFC acceptance
recommendation.body: Keep this PR open and unmerged until maintainers accept or narrow the RFC and the prerequisite lifecycle contract lands.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the assigned reviewer and strongest visible owner of the product-model and authoritative-planning decisions already incorporated into this branch.
